reproducibility_caveat.why_this_matters: The parquet FILE hash recorded below is ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT and must not be used on its own as the reproducibility anchor. pyarrow embeds its own version string in the file (parquet metadata `created_by`), so an identical dataframe serialises to different bytes under different pyarrow versions. A reproducer on another machine would see a hash mismatch and reasonably conclude the reproduction FAILED when the data is in fact identical.
reproducibility_caveat.measured: The original session's split_factors_830.parquet was written by parquet-cpp-arrow 23.0.1 -> file sha256 1f06237a76dd423a...; the re-run here by 21.0.0 -> 0ecea3fc142c9ffc3d.... Data compared directly: same 1,370,220 rows, same 825 tickers, identical route counts (measured 1,369,069 / reconstructed 1,151), and ZERO differing cum_factor values at 9 decimal places. Confirmed separately that pyarrow IS deterministic for a fixed dataframe within one version, so the delta is purely the embedded writer version, not the computation.
reproducibility_caveat.resolution: Each parquet output additionally carries `*.content_sha256`: a fingerprint over values sorted by (ticker, date) with floats rounded to 9dp, which carries no writer metadata and is therefore pyarrow-version independent. VERIFIED to match between the 23.0.1 original and the 21.0.0 re-run. Compare content_sha256 first; treat a file-hash mismatch with a matching content_sha256 as a PASS. split_factor_meta.csv needed no such treatment and matched byte-for-byte, being plain text.
